name: Vehicle Maintenance and Service Eligibility
listdetail: This API provides Toyota and Lexus vehicle maintenance and service program information using the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN). The API is primarily used within the Claims Processing System (CPS) to evaluate vehicle care and maintenance records and determine warranty service eligibility based on applicable maintenance requirements. Users can retrieve information such as the service description, effective and expiration dates, mileage limits, VIN eligibility, oil type, and current service status. The information supports vehicle maintenance evaluation, warranty eligibility decisions, quality reporting, and analysis of vehicle care over time. The Vehicle Repair Details and Service History API provides detailed VIN-based repair history focused on what condition was identified, what caused the issue, and what remedy or repair was performed. This Vehicle Maintenance and Service Eligibility API provides VIN-based maintenance program information focused on service eligibility, coverage effective and expiration dates, mileage limits, oil type, and current service status. The Vehicle Repair Order Summary API provides a summary of recent VIN-based repair orders focused on servicing dealer and personnel, repair activity, labor and parts information, and associated repair costs and payment amounts.

listdetail: This API provides authoritative warranty eligibility determination for a given Vehicle Identification Number (VIN). name: Request for Quote Status and Lifecycle Reporting
listdetail: This API provides access to Request for Quote (RFQ) status and lifecycle data from the Next Generation Purchasing (NGP) system. It enables users to retrieve RFQ records, including status, supplier, part, and organizational attributes, based on configurable query parameters. Users can filter results using Project Code, Buyer Code, and Supplier Code to narrow the dataset to specific sourcing activities, responsible buyers, or suppliers. These parameters allow targeted retrieval of RFQs associated with particular programs, ownership, or supplier relationships. The API returns RFQ records with their current status (e.g., RFQ Prep, RFQ Outstanding, RFQ Received, Approved, Cancelled), along with key lifecycle dates such as issue date, supplier due date, and receipt date. Additional attributes such as quotation type, RFQ type (e.g., OE, Service, Export sourcing), and trigger type provide context on how the RFQ was created and processed within the sourcing workflow. listdetail: This API provides unmatched vehicle arrival audit records from the Toyota Transportation Management System (TTMS), identifying cases where arrival data does not fully align across expected shipment, vehicle, or dealer information. It enables visibility into data discrepancies during vehicle arrival processing, supporting reconciliation and audit workflows across logistics systems. The service returns VIN, shipment ID, dealer code, and audit indicators, along with a timestamp of the most recent update, allowing systems to detect and investigate mismatches between planned and actual arrival data. name: Supplier Parts Master Data Update
listdetail: This API enables authorized suppliers to update existing Parts Master information used by 2-Way Supplier Connectivity (2WSC). 2WSC supports collaboration between Toyota and suppliers by providing visibility into supplier requirements and forecasts, as well as suppliers’ ability to commit to those forecasts. The API allows suppliers to maintain part information for the supplier plants assigned to their account. Updates can include supplier part numbers, capacity factors, configurable custom attributes, and production line assignments. Capacity Factor is used as a multiplier to increase or decrease a part’s forecasted quantity before it is provided to the supplier. Custom Value 1, Custom Value 2, and Custom Value 3 are flexible, supplier-configurable attributes. Suppliers can define the purpose and labels of these fields based on their business needs, such as weight, color, packaging type, or other part-specific information. Each update requires a valid NAMC to identify the appropriate Toyota plant or business line. Suppliers may also optionally associate a part with the specific production line at their facility where the part is produced.

name: Manufacturing Process Risk Assessment

Users can retrieve process details, completed risk assessments, identified hazards, and risk scores and levels. The API also shows how risk levels may change after risk reduction measures are applied. This information can be used to review process risks, research past assessments, support safety analysis, and assist with compliance and reporting activities. The Manufacturing Process and Training Governance API focuses on what the manufacturing process is, how it is structured, and whether team members are trained and qualified to perform it. This Manufacturing Process Risk Assessment API focuses on what safety risks and hazards have been identified for the manufacturing process and how those risks are assessed and reduced.

name: SAP Global Trade Services Part Lookup
listdetail: This API enables users to retrieve SAP Global Trade Services (GTS) part information using a Toyota part number. It provides part master and trade-related data, including part description, sourcing information, pricing, country of origin (COO), Export Control Classification Number (ECCN), and Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) information. This data supports shipping, logistics, and trade compliance activities by providing the information needed to identify, classify, and process parts for shipment. MSRS (Miscellaneous Shipping Request System), a TMNA internal application used for miscellaneous shipments, uses the API to quickly retrieve required part information from SAP GTS. By reducing manual SAP GTS lookups, the API helps streamline shipment processing and provides MSRS with the product, pricing, origin, and trade classification information needed to process miscellaneous shipments without unnecessary delays.

name: Vehicle Invoice Transmission to Toyota Canada
listdetail: This API enables users to transmit electronic vehicle invoice information from Toyota manufacturing operations to Toyota Canada Inc. (TCI) for Accounts Payable processing. When vehicles are delivered from Texas manufacturing operations to TCI, SAP Process Orchestration (SAP PO) uses this API to send an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI 810) invoice containing vehicle and billing information required for financial processing. The invoice includes key details such as VIN, Katashiki, model information, invoice references, payment terms, and related billing data. TCI uses the information received through this API to create payables to Toyota Motor Engineering & Manufacturing North America, Inc. (TEMA), helping automate invoice processing and reduce manual financial transactions between organizations. This API helps finance teams, accounting organizations, manufacturing operations, vehicle distribution teams, and integration teams streamline vehicle invoicing processes and improve billing efficiency. By providing a standardized method for transmitting electronic invoice data between SAP and TCI systems, it supports timely financial reconciliation, reduces manual effort, and enables consistent processing of vehicle delivery transactions. The API is secured using Client ID and Client Secret authentication and serves as a critical integration point for cross-company financial operations.

This Create Planned Maintenance Work Orders API supports scheduled and preventive maintenance activities by generating work orders before maintenance work is performed. The supports corrective maintenance activities by generating work orders for equipment failures, breakdowns, and production issues after an incident has been identified.

name: Vehicle Katashiki – Model Code Mapping
listdetail: This API provides reference data linking Katashiki (vehicle design and manufacturing definition) with Model Codes (vehicle ordering and identification codes). It enables systems to retrieve the attributes associated with each unique Katashiki–Model Code pairing, offering a consolidated view of how vehicles are defined across manufacturing and sales contexts. Because Katashiki and Model Codes have a many-to-many relationship, a single Katashiki can map to multiple Model Codes and vice versa. Each pairing includes key attributes such as model year, Japan model number, family code, division, plant information, status indicators, production timing, and shipping weight. This ensures a consistent and reliable source for vehicle configuration reference. By centralizing these mappings, the API supports alignment across systems and improves the accuracy of reporting, integration, and operational processes.

name: Manufacturing Parts Trade Compliance Tariffs

listdetail: This dataset supports the Tariff Hub initiative by providing summarized trade and tariff information for Toyota’s recent manufacturing parts imports. It enables Corporate Compliance teams to analyze dutiable goods, duty rates, duty amounts, and total paid amounts for Toyota Motor Engineering & Manufacturing (TEMA) and Toyota Motor Sales (TMS). The data is sourced from TradeVault, Toyota’s internal trade data repository maintained by Compliance & Audit (Customs & Trade Compliance). TradeVault integrates information from U.S. Customs & Border Protection, customs brokers, and internal Toyota systems to support accurate trade compliance reporting and oversight. The dataset includes aggregated tariff and entry‑level summaries by Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) code, product category, importer, country of export and origin, mode of transportation, and calendar/fiscal periods. It is designed to support dashboards and analytical reporting related to import volumes, goods values, duty exposure, and duty payments. Use this <strong><a href="https://data.toyota.com/products/dataset/462">Manufacturing Parts Trade Compliance</a></strong> dataset when you need detailed compliance and shipment‑level insight into manufacturing parts imports, including Import Security Filing (ISF) filings, entry types, trade participants, and regulatory execution.

This API streamlines vehicle configuration and order management processes, improving efficiency, consistency, and accuracy across automotive sales and ordering workflows.

name: Electronic Export Information (EEI) Inbound Response
listdetail: This API enables Toyota to manage and exchange export shipment information between internal systems and U.S. customs brokers. Shipment details for parts or products leaving the U.S. are first entered into systems like the Miscellaneous Shipping Request System (MSRS) and then sent to SAP Global Trade Services (GTS), which creates the official export declaration. This API transmits the Electronic Export Information (EEI) from SAP GTS through TradeNext to customs brokers. Once the brokers file the shipment with U.S. customs, they send back confirmation and updates, such as the Internal Transaction Number (ITN), which are processed and updated in SAP GTS to ensure accurate and compliant records. This API is vital for maintaining compliance with U.S. export regulations, preventing shipment delays or penalties, and facilitating smooth communication with customs brokers. It is primarily used by Customs and Trade Compliance (CTC) teams for export approvals, Information Technology (IT) teams for system integration, and customs brokers for filing export documentation. Common use cases include shipping prototype parts, product samples, or other miscellaneous shipments requiring special export approval and customs filing.

Additionally, reporting teams can use the data to analyze trends and improve service workflows, enhancing overall vehicle performance monitoring and communication between service centers and vehicles. This API works in conjunction with the <strong><a href="https://data.toyota.com/products/api/36">Service Connect Remote Vehicle Diagnostics</a></strong> API, which delivers detailed diagnostic information such as Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTC), Freeze Frame Data (FFD), and other vehicle data based on the Request ID and VIN number. Together, these APIs provide a complete remote diagnostics solution, from tracking request status to accessing comprehensive vehicle diagnostic results, enhancing overall vehicle performance monitoring and communication between service centers and vehicles.

name: Workday Employee Search
listdetail: This API provides real-time access to accurate employee job data for internal use by team members and corporate partners. It is commonly integrated into systems such as HR platforms, IT service portals, onboarding tools, and badge access systems. When an employee’s email is submitted through this API, Workday verifies the input and returns relevant job data if a match exists; otherwise, it returns an error or no data. A standard response includes details such as Employee ID, Full Name, Badge ID, Work Email, Phone Number, Job Title, Manager ID, Department, Desk Location, Building ID, and Mail Drop. By centralizing access to this data through Workday, the API improves accuracy, reduces duplication, and enables efficient workflows across enterprise systems that depend on employee information. For comprehensive identity lifecycle management, including retrieving, updating, and onboarding user profiles, please refer to the Employee Identity and Role Management API. For basic employee details like Name, Email, Creation Date, and Group Membership, please refer to the Employee Identity Lookup API.

name: Vehicle Parts Lifecycle Status
listdetail: The Changed Parts Lookup API provides access to the latest version of parts information updated in the system, filtered by date and accessory family code. This API is essential for tracking the status of vehicle parts during their development lifecycle, allowing users to determine whether parts are still in prototype stages or have entered production. Details include family code, group number, development code, part name, part number, supplier code, plant code, production status, and design staff code. Typical use cases for this API include enabling engineering teams to monitor part development progress, supporting manufacturing planning by verifying production readiness, and assisting quality control in identifying parts currently in use versus those still under development. By providing up-to-date part status information, the API helps streamline communication across design, production, and supply chain teams, ensuring efficient vehicle development and manufacturing processes. To monitor Engineering Change Instructions (ECIs) before a part is finalized for production, please refer to the Engineering Change Instructions Tracking API.

name: Vehicle Logistics Management - Sensitive
platform: TBDP (IRM, PASA, C360, Q360, IRM-Pricing, etc.)
listdetail: This dataset provides sensitive pricing, rate, routing, and transportation information related to the movement of vehicles from manufacturing plants and other origin locations to dealerships and distribution destinations. It includes vehicle logistics data from Toyota Logistics System (TLS), vendor partner Integrated Couriers & Logistics (ICL), and trucking, rail, and vessel transportation providers. The dataset provides route-level information including origin and destination locations, dealer information, transportation type, carrier information, transit distance, transit time, and vehicle attributes such as make, model, series, and model year. It also includes detailed transportation pricing and rate components for truck, rail, and vessel movements, including freight rates, tolls, ferry charges, tiered truck rates, customs charges, carbon taxes, and other applicable transportation costs. This data supports vehicle logistics planning, transportation cost analysis, route and carrier analysis, rate validation, and transit-time analysis by providing the information needed to understand vehicle transportation routes, associated rates, and movement requirements from origin to destination. This Vehicle Logistics Management - Sensitive dataset focuses specifically on sensitive vehicle transportation pricing and rate information, including truck, rail, and vessel freight charges, route rates, tolls, and other transportation costs associated with moving vehicles.The Vehicle Logistics Management dataset provides broader operational vehicle logistics information, including vehicle tracking, locations, routes, shipments, carriers, transportation events, estimated arrival times, transit activity, and logistics performance used to manage and monitor vehicle movement.

This data supports vehicle logistics planning, shipment tracking, route analysis, transportation performance analysis, inventory visibility, and monitoring of vehicle movements from origin to destination. name: Vehicle Inspection Data for Transport Tracking
listdetail: This API provides standardized inspection data for vehicles transported via rail, truck, and vessel across multiple Toyota Motor North America (TMNA) locations. It serves as a critical quality assurance tool, ensuring that vehicles meet operational and compliance standards before they are authorized to continue through the supply chain. The API captures detailed information about each inspection event, including the vehicle's unique identification, the mode and type of transport, the specific location where the inspection took place, and identifiers related to the transport and inspection companies involved. It also records the status of the inspection and any indicators of damage. This comprehensive data supports tracking and visibility of vehicle movements, facilitates accurate billing and financial reconciliation, and helps maintain regulatory compliance for vehicle imports and exports. By integrating this inspection data into broader logistics and enterprise systems, organizations can enhance operational efficiency, manage exceptions proactively, and generate valuable insights for continuous improvement.

name: Vehicle Incentive Forecast
platform: TBDP (IRM, PASA, C360, Q360, IRM-Pricing, etc.)
listdetail: This dataset provides vehicle incentive planning and forecasting information used to support the development of effective incentive strategies for upcoming sales periods. It includes anticipated cash incentives, financing and lease incentives, sales forecasts, vehicle pricing, market trends, and competitor incentive information by vehicle model or series. The dataset combines historical and current incentive activity with vehicle sales, Manufacturer's Suggested Retail Price (MSRP), competitor activity, market trends, and incentive elasticity information to support analysis of how changes in pricing and incentives may influence vehicle sales and market response. It also includes Toyota and Lexus incentive proposals, national incentive information, forecast and budget data, product health measures, and regional and vehicle-level details where available. This data supports incentive planning, forecasting, budgeting, competitive analysis, and market response analysis by providing the information needed to evaluate historical incentive performance, compare Toyota and Lexus vehicles with competitors, forecast future incentive requirements, and understand the relationship between incentive spending, vehicle pricing, and expected sales performance.

name: Vehicle Details
listdetail: The Vehicle Details API provides comprehensive vehicle information, Retail Delivery Record (RDR) details, and Deal Finalization Portal (DFP) data through the Dealer Daily Open Access (DDOA) system. This service facilitates seamless data exchange between Toyota Motor Sales (TMS) and Dealership Management Systems (DMS), enabling dealers to access and transmit critical vehicle and sales data efficiently. In the context of vehicle incentives, the API ensures that dealers can submit and verify key components necessary for incentive eligibility. The "Deal" is a combination of the RDR, Incentive, and Toyota Financial Services (TFS) Credit Contract, when applicable. For a dealer to qualify for an incentive, all three components must match precisely. If any of these elements—the RDR, Incentive, or TFS Credit Contract—fail to align, the dealer will not be eligible for incentive payment. By leveraging the Vehicle Details API, dealerships can streamline their processes, eliminate discrepancies, and ensure that incentive payments are accurately processed for eligible dealers.

name: Vehicle Configuration and Reprice
listdetail: Through this API, a comprehensive list of VINs will be provided via XML for which price changes are expected to be made across a group of vehicles within a given phase code for Private Distributors (Southeast Toyota Distributors (SET) and Gulf State Toyota Distributors (GST). Toyota Motor Sales, USA, Inc. (TMS) provides all levels of cost and pricing of the Model, the Factory-installed accessories, and the Post Production Options (PPOs) at the time of its initial vehicle configuration. This Reprice API service makes it possible to do simulation and updates for vehicle repositioning and vehicle windfall pricing whenever it is needed. Repositioning is a process by which business users can update the cost and pricing of the Model and factory-installed accessories of one or more vehicle series from an existing cost and price general increment (GI) phase code to another. A windfall is the result of a drop in cost and pricing of a vehicle series. To track and respond to real-time configuration and pricing updates, use the Vehicle Configuration and Pricing Change Notification API. To find detailed configuration data (series, specs, etc.) for vehicles after a specified date, please refer to the Vehicle Configuration and Accessory Changes API.

name: Trouble Code Transmission for Maintenance Events
listdetail: This API enables remote transmission of Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs) for a specific vehicle identified by its Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) when a required maintenance event is triggered. It includes key information such as service codes, system details, Engine Control Unit (ECU) identifiers, mileage, and event timestamps to ensure accurate tracking of vehicle issues. When triggered, the API sends a sequence of DTCs to the Product Quality and Service Support (PQSS) team, ensuring that the diagnostic information is logged for further quality campaign management and reporting. To view all DTCs not triggered by a maintenance event for a specific VIN in Data Hub (DH), refer to the Trouble Code Prioritization API. For the outcome of monitored ECU values based on a VIN, view the Electronic Control Unit Monitoring Results API. For comprehensive remote vehicle diagnostics, including DTCs and Freeze Frame Data (FFD), refer to the Service Connect Remote Vehicle Diagnostics API. To access a list of ECU values for a specific VIN, including last acquisition mileage, date, ECU values, and network target address, consult the Service Connect Electronic Control Unit Values List API. For Freeze Frame Data (FFD) in relation to specific DTCs for monitoring quality and initiating recalls, please refer to the Freeze Frame Data Transmission for Vehicle Quality Monitoring API. To view vehicle usage patterns and customer behavior over time, please refer to the Driving Behavior Analytics API.

name: Toyota In-Market Models
listdetail: The Toyota In-Market Models predict how likely a customer is to purchase a Toyota vehicle by a specific series or segment type within the next 12 months. This applies to current Toyota owners and those who previously owned a Toyota in the last 15 years, but no longer own one today. These models help Marketing teams plan and execute in-market campaigns to existing customers and their lookalikes. It also helps optimize media-spend by enabling targeted marketing. For customers predicted to be in-market, each model will return the probability that the customer will purchase a particular series or vehicle segment. Using this probability, we can determine how strong a customer''s in-market signal is. Depending on the business use case, the customer''s signal strength enables strategies that target only the most in-market customers. All the models consist of Machine Learning (ML) data based on patterns & trends. Some of the most significant data sources for building these models are Customer Demographics Data, Toyota Service History USA, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data, Vehicle Configuration Data, and New Car Sales VIN Based Actuals Data.

name: Toyota Customer Loyalty Models
listdetail: The Toyota Customer Loyalty Models predict the probability of a customer returning for a service or purchase of a new vehicle. This is relevant for all customers who currently own or have owned a Toyota in the past. Customers who repair or buy parts from a Toyota Dealer have a higher likelihood of buying another Toyota or Lexus vehicle. There are currently four models available for this feature. Model 1: Toyota Return to Service Visit Model (Binary) This is a binary classifier that predicts if a customer will return to an authorized service center for service. Model 2: Toyota Return to Service Revenue Model (5 Class Multi-class) This is a multi-class classifier that predicts the spending potential of a customer after the customer is predicted to return for a service. This generates the probabilities for 5 different classes and based on the highest probability the customer is predicted for the given class. Model 3: Toyota Return to Purchase Visit Model (Binary) This is a binary classifier that predicts the probability of a customer returning to purchase a new vehicle. Model 4: Toyota Return to Purchase Revenue Model (6 Class Multi-class) This is a multi-class classifier that predicts the spending potential of a customer after the customer is predicted to return for a purchase of a new vehicle. This generates the probabilities for 6 different classes. A final spending value is predicted after complex data processing considering probabilities for all classes and their average purchase value. Some of the most important data sources for building these models are Customer Demographics Data, Toyota Service History USA, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data.

name: TMMK-PWT Conveyance Night Letter Reports

This report is essential to Conyenance team members in order to monitor their progress toward daily targets and KPIs across shifts. The Conveyance team has a process performed at the end of each shift that records KPIs as noted in each Night Letter report. KPIs in the Night Letter include Order Finish / Last Unload, Overseas Taps, Overseas Overflow Maintenance, Hot Calls, and more.

name: TMMI West Paint Dashboard
listdetail: This dashboard provides an array of in-depth Toyota Motor Manufacturing, Indiana, Inc. (TMMI) West Paint reports containing information on equipment and operations essential for cost efficiency, process planning, increasing safety and productivity, improving on-time delivery, and analyzing trends. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM01 Cost Analysis by Equipment: The following report provides an overview of the costs associated with equipment. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM02 Detail Cost Analysis by Equipment Report: This report breaks down the previous list into a more detailed description of what we spent on certain equipment assets. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM03 Faults 10 to 19 Minutes Line Report: This report provides a list of all Faults that occur between 10 - 19 minutes. If a Fault lasts longer than 19 minutes, it becomes a larger issue causing extended downtime and should be escalated to a priority for repairs. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM04 Process Report: This report shows a breakdown of all the processes at the facility, along with the associated Equipment Stops and Line Stops. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM05 Major Breakdown Faults Report: This report lists the major breakdowns (anything over 19 minutes), the Build Date Start, the Line Stop, the Equipment Stop, and the Fault description. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM06 West Paint Equipment Summary Report: This report provides the number of Faults, Line Stops, and Equipment Stops across all equipment on-site. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM07 Repetitive Faults Report: This report is meant to capture repetitive equipment Faults so that we can track and resolve repair issues. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM08 Summary Floor Conveyor Report: This report contains a list of floor conveyor groups and the total amount of equipment Faults and Line Stops. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM09 Totals of All Equipment Detail Report Production: This report breaks down all equipment into major areas with the total number of Faults, Stop times, and an explanation of each Fault during production hours. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM10 Totals of All Equipment Details Report: This report breaks down all equipment into major areas with the total number of Faults, Stop times, and an explanation of each Fault that occurred throughout the entire work day. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM11 Totals of All Non-Equipment Details Report: Similar to the previous report but lists Non-Equipment downtime with the total number of Faults, Stop times, and an explanation of each Fault that occurred outside of active production. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM12 Totals Floor Conveyor Detail Report: This report contains a list of floor conveyors, along with the total amount of equipment Faults and Line Stops. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM13 Totals Robot Detail Report: It contains information about the robots on the floor, as well as Faults, Stop times, and Work Order descriptions.

name: TIPS - Third Party Notifications
listdetail: The Toyota Integrated Privacy System (TIPS) Third Party Notifications API enables approved external entities such as vendors, partners, and service providers to notify Toyota of opt-out requests they receive directly from consumers. This ensures that privacy preferences shared with third parties are also respected within Toyota’s systems, reinforcing a consistent and unified privacy posture. When a third party processes a consumer’s opt-out or “Do Not Sell or Share My Information” request, this API is used to communicate that action to TIPS. By doing so, it helps prevent unnecessary sharing or visibility of the consumer’s personal information, providing an added layer of customer privacy protection beyond Toyota's direct interactions.

name: TIPS - Response
listdetail: This API enables Toyota Motor North America (TMNA) and its affiliates to respond to California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) requests efficiently and securely. It sends Data Subject Access Request (DSAR) responses toTIPS, which tracks and manages these consumer privacy requests. Integrated with OneTrust for privacy management and Experian for identity verification, the API supports key CCPA rights such as the Right to Know, Right to Opt-out, and Right to Delete personal data. The API ensures TMNA’s Data Systems, Compliance, Privacy, Legal, and TIPS Teams can process these requests in compliance with privacy laws, protecting consumer rights and Toyota’s reputation.

listdetail: The Toyota Integrated Privacy System (TIPS) Global Privacy Control API is designed to capture and process real-time privacy preference signals such as the “Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information” request sent directly from a user’s browser or device. These signals are part of emerging privacy frameworks like the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) and its amendments (e.g., CPRA), as well as similar laws in Colorado, Connecticut, Texas, and Montana. When a user enables GPC in their browser or through a consent platform, this API receives the signal and logs the request into TIPS, initiating a privacy action such as opt-out of data sale or sharing. It serves as the entry point for honoring automated privacy choices and supports Toyota’s compliance with GPC requirements.

name: Supplier Skid and Box Details
listdetail: This API serves as a communication channel between the Toyota Shipping Confirmation System (TSCS) and downstream logistics systems, including Freight Verification Module (FVM), Internal Logistics Management System (ILMS), Trade Compliance, and external systems such as Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada’s Material Information Tracking solution. The API provides detailed planned shipment information at both the skid (pallet) and box levels, enabling logistics teams, suppliers, and internal systems to coordinate manufacturing parts shipments before transportation activities begin. The API supports two key functions. First, it provides skid-level shipment details, including pallet, order, supplier, plant, dock, Radio Frequency Identification (RFID), and route information used for logistics planning and shipment tracking. Second, it provides box-level shipment details, including kanban, part number, quantity-per-container (QPC), manifest, and line-side delivery information that improves visibility into shipment contents and processing requirements. By providing detailed planned shipment data before pallet building, loading, pickup, and transportation occur, the API establishes the foundation for the manufacturing parts logistics process and enables efficient coordination across Toyota's supply chain network.

name: Supplier Pallet Build and Load Shipment Confirmation
listdetail: This API uses the Logistics Input Output System (LIOS) to exchange shipment confirmation data between the Shipping Confirmation System (SCS) and Warehouse Management System (WMS). The API enables suppliers, warehouse operations teams, and Toyota logistics teams to confirm pallet builds and shipment loading activities, ensuring that manufacturing parts shipments are accurately documented and processed before transportation begins. The API supports two key logistics processes. First, suppliers submit pallet build information after assembling pallets for production orders, including part, kanban, box, skid, and Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) details. Second, suppliers submit trailer load information after completing shipment loading activities for a route or trailer. Toyota processes the submitted data and returns confirmation numbers or error messages, providing verification that shipment information has been successfully received and recorded. By validating pallet builds and shipment loads before pickup occurs, the API helps improve shipment accuracy, inventory visibility, logistics coordination, and transportation readiness across the manufacturing supply chain.

name: Supplier Invoice Validation
listdetail: This API enables seamless validation and unblocking of supplier invoices within the SAP system by integrating with Pegaso’s PAC-validated XML data. Proveedor Autorizado de Certificación (PAC) ensures that invoices comply with legal and tax regulations before they are accepted and processed by businesses and government systems. When Pegaso receives an invoice from a supplier, it sends detailed invoice and shipment information to SAP through this API. SAP uses this data to verify invoice authenticity, unblock validated invoices, and authorize them for payment. This process ensures that only compliant and accurate invoices proceed through payment cycles, reinforcing internal financial controls and reducing manual errors. Key use cases include invoice validation, shipment verification, invoice unblocking, and payment authorization. The API supports accounts payable teams, finance and compliance officers, SAP integrators, and procurement departments by automating invoice processing and maintaining alignment with corporate financial policies. Ultimately, it accelerates payment workflows and enhances accuracy in supplier invoice management. The Payment Complement Reporting Tracker API focuses on reporting and validating payment complements after payments are made, ensuring compliance with Mexican tax authority requirements for payment documentation. To reconcile and compare posted invoices between SAP and Ariba, please refer to the Supplier Invoice Reconciliation API.

listdetail: This API provides access to service operation code information stored in the Claims Processing System (CPS) for Toyota and Lexus vehicles. It is primarily used to retrieve recall and campaign operation details for a specific Vehicle Identification Number (VIN). This data supports accurate tracking of vehicle repairs, technician labor, and campaign execution status across the service network. The API can return multiple records per VIN, as a single vehicle may be subject to more than one campaign or recall. Users can only view closed recalls after the repair has been completed. For this to occur, the claim for the repair must already be submitted, and the dealer's repair order must be fully closed. Once the dealer completes the repair via a Repair Order and submits a Warranty Claim, the relevant recall information becomes accessible, ensuring that all necessary data is available for effective tracking and management of service campaigns.

name: Smart Window ETA Model
listdetail: The Smart Window ETA model predicts when a vehicle will be delivered to the dealer at various stages of its lifecycle, starting with dealer assignment and continuing until it is delivered to the dealer. By using a predictive ETA, we can reduce wasted overhead and transportation delays, as well as make informed decisions concerning inventory planning. The delivery window is updated at major manufacturing and transportation events to provide an accurate estimated delivery window at dealerships from the time of dealer assignment through the manufacturing process and transportation journey. This algorithm is based on Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (UETA) data using events from the most recent 90 days for hundreds of vehicles. Only valid VINs were analyzed during data processing (i.e. those with a valid delivery code). Traded vehicles are taken into account only once they have been delivered for the first time. Any VINs with a "hold" have been filtered out. A tree-based modeling approach has been used to predict time-to-delivery from events received for each VIN. The clusters of points obtained at different leaf nodes of the CART decision tree were explored during this process. Using a typical tree-based model, the prediction outcome is an aggregated value of observations at the leaf node. However, our analysis showed that observations at the leaf nodes are not necessarily homogeneous and follow a gamma distribution. By aggregating all of those values, hidden trends in those distributions would be masked. Therefore, we regressed the "time-to-delivery" against deciles of distributions. At leaf node, minimum window refers to absolute minimum value, and maximum window refers to x-intersection of decile regression line at one. The model predicts each VIN's every event (limited to only post-FQA events in phase 1), where a window is provided. It is most likely that vehicles will be delivered between the Start Date and the End Date of windows.

name: Sirius XM BlueTooth Activation Status
listdetail: This API can provide you with status information on Toyota and Lexus Sirius XM customers based on the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN). This information can provide insight to whether a customer was able to successfully set up their Sirius XM Activation using their BlueTooth, and the current status of their account. When a customer wants to sign up with Sirius XM, they need a Radio ID number to enroll. The Data Communication Module (DCM) processes an Activation Response from Sirius XM for the End User. The End User receives Sirius XM Activation Instructions and their personal Radio ID (also called ESN or SID). The End User can use their Radio ID to register the radio in their name and set up their account.

name: Shipment Equipment Status and Location Update
listdetail: This API communicates real-time updates to the Warehouse Management System (WMS) when there is a change to a trailer or container’s status or parking location. It provides outbound shipment data including container number, equipment ID, seal number, Standard Carrier Alpha Code (SCAC), shipment ID, loaded quantity, total weight, and hazmat indicator. Each message includes a timestamp and key identifiers for the sender, receiver, and organization such as the North American Parts Center (NAPC). This API supports outbound logistics operations by ensuring accurate and timely equipment and shipment status reporting during the packing and loading process. To monitor trailer flow within the yard and dock area, including when and where a trailer arrives, is docked, or leaves, please refer to the Trailer Status API.

name: Service Connect Remote Vehicle Diagnostics
listdetail: This API provides the complete vehicle diagnostics information, remotely, based on the Request ID and VIN number. It requests information from Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTC), Freeze Frame Data (FFD) and the last file from the vehicle that has not been uploaded. It returns the Request ID, outcome of the request, Requestor ID and Requestor Application. This API works in conjunction with the Telematics Diagnostics Status API, which tracks and monitors the status and progress of remote diagnostics requests. Together, these APIs offer a comprehensive remote diagnostics solution, enabling service centers to both monitor the request lifecycle and access detailed vehicle diagnostic data, thereby improving early issue detection, maintenance efficiency, and communication between vehicles and service teams. To access a list of ECU values for a specific VIN, including last acquisition mileage, date, ECU values, and network target address, consult the Service Connect Electronic Control Unit Values List API. To view all DTCs not triggered by a maintenance event for a specific VIN in Data Hub (DH), refer to the Trouble Code Prioritization API. The Trouble Code Transmission for Maintenance Events API focuses on transmitting diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) that are triggered by specific maintenance events. For the outcome of monitored ECU values based on a VIN, view the Electronic Control Unit Monitoring Results API. For Freeze Frame Data (FFD) in relation to specific DTCs for monitoring quality and initiating recalls, please refer to the Freeze Frame Data Transmission for Vehicle Quality Monitoring API.

name: Salvage Status and Warranty Eligibility
listdetail: This API is designed to identify vehicles that are no longer eligible for warranty coverage due to their salvage status. A salvage Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) indicates a vehicle that has been declared a total loss, typically because repair costs exceed its value. This API plays a critical role in helping Toyota eliminate unnecessary warranty payments by shutting off coverage on ineligible vehicles. Warranty Operations use it to block invalid claims, while Service and Field teams confirm coverage before repairs. Dealers can use this service to validate warranty eligibility, helping streamline dealership operations and reduce claim rejections. By integrating this API into their systems and workflows, these teams can enhance operational efficiency, reduce cost leakage, and uphold the integrity of Toyota’s warranty programs.

name: Sales Order Batch Processing
listdetail: This API facilitates asynchronous batch handling, creation, and processing of sales orders within the SAP system for vehicles, parts, and services. By decoupling order submission from immediate processing, it optimizes system performance and enables SAP to handle high transaction volumes without sacrificing responsiveness or stability. When a sales order request is received, the API quickly returns a confirmation number. The complete order creation and processing then take place later in the background through SAP batch jobs or queues. This asynchronous design helps Finance and Accounting teams by ensuring reliable order intake while preventing system bottlenecks during peak times. Orders can include detailed information such as vehicle identification numbers (VINs), purchase order details, customer data, financial amounts, dealer charges, quantities, billing descriptions, sold-to customer accounts, and the originating system or channel. By leveraging this API, organizations can streamline sales order management, reduce manual effort, and maintain SAP system performance under heavy load ensuring timely and accurate processing of vehicle, parts, and service orders.

name: Sales Forecast and Elasticity Model
listdetail: The Sales Forecast and Elasticity Model is a data science tool developed to help Toyota and Lexus sales teams make informed decisions about how much of a discount or financial incentive to offer customers when buying or leasing a vehicle. At its core, the model uses historical sales data and pricing trends to predict how many vehicles are likely to be sold in the future. It also measures how sensitive customers are to changes in price (known as price elasticity) at the Series, Model Year, and Region level. In addition to predicting future sales, the model also compares those predictions with actual sales results to improve its accuracy over time. It uses reliable inputs like forecast cut-off dates, past volumes, pre-incentive prices, and historical performance data to ensure the recommendations are realistic. This system allows the sales teams to explore “what-if” scenarios to prepare for different market conditions whether demand is rising, competition is offering aggressive discounts, or inventory levels are changing.

listdetail: This API delivers information on active service contracts for Safeguard products associated with a specific Vehicle Identification Number (VIN). Safeguard represents one of the protection plans offered through Toyota Financial Services (TFS) to customers and dealers in the United States. As a service mark of Toyota Motor Credit Corporation (TMCC) and Toyota Motor Insurance Services (TMIS), Safeguard coverage may include products like tire and wheel protection, paintless dent repair, key replacement, etc . When a valid VIN is submitted, the API returns details about any applicable Safeguard contracts; if no products are found, the response will indicate that no product is available for the vehicle.

name: Retrieve Operational Dealership Reports
listdetail: This API is a service that retrieves various dealership-related reports from Toyota's Legacy systems. Used by dealer portals, internal systems, and back-office applications, the API serves as a bridge between modern platforms and mainframe-generated reports including data on parts, warranty, finance, vehicle management, and more. Applications such as the Dealer Portal send a Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP) request to the API with key parameters such as Dealer Number, Report Type, and Transaction Date. The API then queries the Seasonally Adjusted Annual Rate (SAAR) host system and returns either the report data or a URL to the HTML-formatted report for display or download. Despite its Legacy status, the API remains in use because the underlying data still resides in Information Management System (IMS), hence the reports are standardized and pre-validated across the dealer network.

name: Retrieve Customer Subscription Portfolio
listdetail: This API provides a detailed overview of all product subscriptions associated with a specific customer and their vehicle. Using the Customer ID and Vehicle Identification Number (VIN), this API returns customer information (e.g., name, type), the total number of active product subscriptions, and for each product, details such as product name, effective and expiration dates, expiration mileage (if applicable), and the associated dealer information. It also outlines the product plan or agreement, which defines what the customer has purchased, for how long, and under what terms. This API is primarily used for lifecycle management, service planning, and customer engagement, giving internal teams and dealer systems a complete view of the customer's subscription portfolio.

name: Retrieve Active Employee Work Schedule
listdetail: This API, part of the Team Member Rotation Application (TMRA) manufacturing portal, retrieves the active work schedule for plant employees within the manufacturing job process area. It provides detailed information about the employee’s assigned date, shift, job area, and specific work tasks during the defined submission period (the timeframe for which the schedule is valid and applicable). The response also includes the total working minutes allocated on a particular production line and job. This API supports TMRA’s goal of optimizing workforce rotation by providing accurate, timely scheduling data for effective team member assignment and workload management during the submission period.

name: Retention Parts Propensity Models
listdetail: Retention Parts Propensity Models are available for batteries, brakes, wipers, tires, and oil. Through these models, it is possible to anticipate which vehicles might need a specific part and to communicate with the customer in a timely manner. This helps optimize marketing, improve customer experience for Parts and Service marketing campaigns, and retain customer loyalty. Email campaigns support email marketing efforts for these parts-related campaigns by predicting which customers are most likely to purchase the respective key retention part. Digital campaigns support Digital marketing efforts for parts-related campaigns which are conducted on various Toyota websites or social media platforms. All the key parts of Propensity Models are utilized by media agencies to derive strategies around audiences generated by these models. The Retention Parts Propensity Models are relevant to all customers who have owned or previously owned a Toyota or Lexus. These models predict a likely outcome at the customer level and can be used for a wide variety of business operations. From millions of existing Toyota customers, these models identify only those who are most likely to require retention parts. Data collected from a broad range of sources is used in all of the models to study patterns and trends. Some of the most important data sources for building these models are Toyota Service History USA, Lexus Service History USA, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data, Vehicle Configuration Data, Direct Parts Specifications and Tracking . Datasets like these are crucial to building hundreds of features for training models. For more details, please contact the Customer Data Science (CUDS) team. These Propensity Models predict how likely it is that a customer will visit a Toyota dealership for these specific retention parts within the next month. Each propensity score is calculated at VIN level and a customer can likely have different scores for each VIN owned. A binary prediction value of 1 means that the VIN/Customer is predicted to purchase the specific retention part within a month, while a binary prediction value of 0 means that the VIN/Customer is not likely to purchase the particular part.

name: Reserve Vehicle
listdetail: The Reserve Vehicle service, also referred to as Vehicle Reserve Inventory, enables dealerships to efficiently manage vehicle reservations for their customers. This API allows dealers to reserve vehicles allocated to their dealership in various categories: A (vehicles on Order or Assigned), F (vehicles In Transit), and G (vehicles In Stock). name: Repair and Maintenance Records
listdetail: This API provides a comprehensive service history for Toyota and Lexus vehicles using the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN). This API is primarily used within the Claims Processing System (CPS) to evaluate vehicle care and maintenance records. It enables quality teams such as Product Quality & Service Support (PQSS) to monitor how vehicles are maintained over time, which supports quality reporting, insights for future vehicle builds, and proactive service recommendations. CPS also uses this data to determine warranty service eligibility by assessing whether a vehicle has been properly maintained according to recommended schedules. The service history includes details such as the type of service performed, effective and expiration dates, mileage limits, oil type, and current warranty status. To check past repair orders for warranty claim validation and approval, please refer to the Warranty Eligibility and Service History API.

name: Private Distributor Monroney Image
listdetail: This API helps Private Distributors (PDs) correctly set up the most updated version of Monroney images so they can efficiently generate Monroney labels for Toyota vehicles. As a legally binding document, the Monroney label must have specific and accurate information before it can be affixed to new vehicles. This API provides the correct set up for basic Vehicle Data, Standard Equipment language, Crash Test Rating information from the New Car Assessment Program (NCAP), and Fuel Economy and Miles per Gallon (mpg) information from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). PDs can generate the Monroney image, add Post Production Options (PPOs), total MSRP, shipping and final Dealer Destination information, and then print the final Monroney label. This API supports the following distributors: - Gulf States Toyota (GST) - South East Toyota (SET) Toyota de Puerto Rico (TdPR) should use the Monroney Configuration Images API . Foreign distributors are not currently included.

name: Payment Complement Reporting Tracker
listdetail: This API provides detailed information on payments made by Toyota manufacturing plants in Mexico to their local vendors, ensuring compliance with Mexican tax regulations. In Mexico, companies must validate customer invoices with the tax authority Servicio de Administración Tributaria (SAT) through an authorized certification provider (Proveedor Autorizado de Certificación, PAC). The API integrates with SAP’s Document Reporting and Compliance (DRC) solution and the PAC service via Pegaso, enabling automated transmission and validation of payment complements as XML eDocuments. A payment complement is an official electronic document that records payments related to invoices, providing details such as amounts paid, payment dates, and invoice references to ensure regulatory compliance. Key data provided includes issuer and receiver details, Registro Federal de Contribuyentes (RFC) tax identification number, payment and invoice amounts, currency, payment method, document numbers, company codes, and payment dates, ensuring transparency and regulatory compliance in Mexico’s payment processes. The Supplier Invoice Validation API ensures that supplier invoices are validated and unblocked in SAP before payment, focusing on invoice authenticity and compliance. To reconcile and compare posted invoices between SAP and Ariba, please refer to the Supplier Invoice Reconciliation API.

name: Parts Order Management
listdetail: This API is an integral component of the Advanced Parts System (APS), designed to assist authorized dealers in efficiently managing their parts orders submitted through the Dealer Daily platform. This API provides dealers with the ability to view the current status and details of their submitted parts orders, modify order specifics such as quantities, items, or shipping preferences, and upgrade orders for expedited processing or alternative fulfillment options. Additionally, it allows for the cancellation of parts orders in cases of changes or errors prior to fulfillment. Typical use cases for this API include scenarios where a dealer checks the fulfillment status of a pending order, updates an order to accommodate new vehicle service needs, requests an expedited shipping upgrade for a high-priority part, or cancels a mistakenly submitted order before processing. By integrating with APS, this API ensures real-time access to order information and transactional flexibility, helping streamline parts inventory management and improve order accuracy.

name: Parts Distribution Center Lane Assignment
listdetail: This API is designed to manage and track lane assignments within a Parts Distribution Center (PDC) using the Container Control Tower (CCT) system. It provides detailed information about how containers or parts are routed through specific lanes in the distribution center, facilitating efficient handling and movement of inventory. The API response includes metadata such as the number of lane assignment records returned, a status code and message indicating the success of the request, a unique transaction identifier (GUID), and a timestamp marking when the response was generated. The core of the response is an array of lane assignment items, each representing a specific lane action. This comprehensive data supports real-time visibility and control over container movements within the PDC, ensuring that parts are accurately routed to their next destination, such as dealerships or other facilities.

Furthermore, insights from this API assist Toyota in identifying opportunities to optimize hydrogen fueling infrastructure by analyzing rental patterns and station downtime, thereby enhancing customer satisfaction and supporting the broader adoption of hydrogen fuel cell technology.

name: Mirai Loaner Rental Status and Claims Tracking
listdetail: Using the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN), this API delivers real-time status updates and remaining rental day details for vehicles enrolled in the Mirai Loaner Program. This API enables dealers and program administrators to efficiently monitor loaner vehicle usage, availability, and claim processing, ensuring seamless management of the program. The Mirai Loaner Program offers temporary replacement vehicles exclusively from the new and unlicensed MY25 Mirai lineup, including demonstration models with 20,000 miles or less. Eligible vehicles must be purchased or leased directly from dealer ground stock inventory within the program period and registered with the California State Department of Motor Vehicles. The program runs from August 5, 2025, through September 2, 2025. All credit applications related to the program require approval by Toyota Financial Services (TFS). The Claims Processing System (CPS) integrated with this API manages and tracks claims associated with loaner vehicles, including rental days, sublet types, invoice amounts, and rental reasons. By providing a centralized platform for claim data, CPS supports accurate billing, reimbursement, and compliance with program eligibility requirements. Overall, this API streamlines the administration of the Mirai Loaner Program by combining real-time vehicle status monitoring with comprehensive claims processing, enhancing dealer efficiency and customer satisfaction while promoting Toyota’s commitment to sustainable hydrogen fuel cell technology.

name: Mileage Estimator
listdetail: The Mileage Estimator model estimates miles for each VIN at the end of the current month and the end of the following month. It can also forecast the mileage of each VIN for the next six months. This model allows Parts and Services marketing campaigns to target customers based on their mileages. It can also be used for understanding the average VIN miles at the Regional or National level for each Series Type. Additionally, it assists with In-Market Campaigns by identifying the age of the VIN. Data collected from a broad range of sources is used in all of the models to study patterns and trends. Some of the most important data sources for building these models are Toyota Service History USA, Lexus Service History USA, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data, and Vehicle Configuration Data. Based on historical trends, it takes into account specific Series, Model Year, and time-since-first-use combinations, as well as industry averages, standard grids, and miles driven since recent service visits by VIN. Subcomponents of this feature are comprised of Standard Vehicle Miles Grids that have been combined in various ways. Before returning a final estimate at the VIN level, the Mileage Estimator model often refers to these standard grids and industry averages. With this feature, you can perform advanced backfilling and exponential smoothing, making it extremely reliable. The feature is currently available for all Toyota VINs (including Scions) with a Date Of First Use within the last 15 years. Lexus VINs are not included. Presently, this feature covers approximately 30 million VINs. Standard Vehicle Miles Grid 1 - This grid is built at Make, Series, Model Year, Months Since DOFU, Percentiles (0-100), and studies the last 15 years of service history. This grid has a miles smoothing mechanism across months-since-DOFU and percentiles. Standard Vehicle Miles Grid 2 - This grid is built at Make, Series, Months Since DOFU, Percentiles (0-100) combination, and studies the last 15+ years of service history. This grid does back-filling of miles at different percentiles and months since DOFU. Once the backfilling is complete, a miles smoothing mechanism is applied across months-since-DOFU and percentiles. Additionally, the grid forecasts the future for the next six months.

name: Logistics Driver Validation and Route Tracking
listdetail: This API enables the Toyota Shipping Confirmation System (TSCS) and logistics providers to validate authorized drivers and confirm supplier pickup activities for manufacturing parts shipments. The API uses invitation codes to verify driver eligibility before shipment pickup and provides route confirmation details that help ensure transportation activities are properly documented and executed according to plan. By supplying a driver invitation token, users can validate drivers against preapproved invitation codes maintained within the logistics network. The API also provides route information, pickup and unload schedules, supplier details, shipment status indicators, and skid tracking information, giving logistics teams visibility into pickup execution and shipment readiness. By confirming driver authorization and pickup activity at the beginning of the transportation process, the API helps improve shipment accuracy, strengthen logistics controls, and ensure that only approved drivers participate in manufacturing parts transportation operations.

name: Lexus In-Market Models
listdetail: The Lexus In-Market Models predict how likely a customer is to purchase a Lexus vehicle by a specific series or segment type within the next 6 months. This applies to current Lexus owners and those who previously owned a Lexus in the last 15 years, but no longer own one today. These models help Marketing teams plan and execute in-market campaigns to existing customers and their lookalikes. It also helps optimize media-spend by enabling targeted marketing. For customers predicted to be in-market, each model will return the probability that the customer will purchase a particular series or vehicle segment. Using this probability, we can determine how strong a customer''s in-market signal is in real-time. Depending on the business use case, the customer''s signal strength enables strategies that target only the most in-market customers. There are currently four models available for this feature. LUV : the likelihood that a customer will purchase a new NX, RX, GX, or LX Sedan : the likelihood that a customer will purchase a new IS, ES, GS, LS, RC, LC, HS, SC, CT, LFA CPO LUV : the likelihood that a customer will purchase a certified pre-owned NX, RX, GX, or LX CPO Sedan : the likelihood that a customer will purchase a certified pre-owned IS, ES, GS, LS, RC, LC, HS, SC, CT, LFA All the models consist of Machine Learning (ML) data based on patterns & trends. Some of the most significant data sources for building these models are Customer Demographics Data, Lexus Service History USA, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data, Vehicle Configuration Data, and New Car Sales VIN Based Actuals Data.

name: Lexus Customer Loyalty Models
listdetail: The Lexus Customer Loyalty Models predict the probability of a customer returning for a service or purchase of a new Lexus vehicle. This is relevant for all customers who currently own or have owned a Lexus in the past. Customers who repair or buy parts from a Lexus Dealer have a higher likelihood of buying another Lexus vehicle. In this feature, there are two different stages: Owner Segmentation and Predictive Modeling. Owner Segmentation: Lexus owners are segmented based on their current relationship and recent activities with Lexus Dealerships. Predictive Modeling: Predicts the likelihood that a Lexus customer will return for purchase or service, as well as future growth potential at a customer level. \n\nSome of the most important data sources for building this model are Customer Demographics Data, Lexus Service History USA, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data, and Customer Call Center.

name: Job Process Performance
platform: TBDP (IRM, PASA, C360, Q360, IRM-Pricing, etc.)
listdetail: This dataset provides manufacturing job, team member rotation, and scheduling data used to understand how work is performed on the production floor and how job assignments are planned across plants, shops, lines, and shifts. The data supports analysis of who performs which jobs, when they are performed, and how often, with a focus on ergonomic impact and job rotation planning. Sourced primarily from the Team Member Rotation Application (TMRA), the dataset includes job definitions, hierarchies, team member assignments, attendance and absences, generated schedules, rotation violations, cumulative job frequency, high‑burden job indicators, training history, and manpower andon activity. It is used to assess ergonomic exposure, identify repetitive or high‑burden work, and support rotation strategies to reduce repetitive action injuries. Future integrations may extend job instruction detail through Toyota Element Instruction Sheet (TEIS) and Qualias. The Job Process Performance Sensitive dataset extends the non‑sensitive version by including individual team member information, such as team member identifiers, attendance and absence records, training history, job versatility, high‑burden job indicators, detailed schedule assignments, schedule violations, manpower andon activity, and user access mappings.

Sourced primarily from the Team Member Rotation Application (TMRA), the dataset includes job definitions, hierarchies, team member assignments, attendance and absences, generated schedules, rotation violations, cumulative job frequency, high‑burden job indicators, training history, and manpower andon activity. It is used to assess ergonomic exposure, identify repetitive or high‑burden work, and support rotation strategies to reduce repetitive action injuries. Future integrations may extend job instruction detail through Toyota Element Instruction Sheet (TEIS) and Qualias. The Job Process Performance Sensitive dataset extends the non‑sensitive version by including individual team member information, such as team member identifiers, attendance and absence records, training history, job versatility, high‑burden job indicators, detailed schedule assignments, schedule violations, manpower andon activity, and user access mappings.

name: Freeze Frame Data Transmission for Vehicle Quality Monitoring
listdetail: This API provides a snapshot of Freeze Frame Data (FFD) related to vehicle quality issues that were identified by the Trouble Code Transmission for Maintenance Events API. It sends key diagnostic information to the PQSS (Product Quality and Service Support) team, which allows them to monitor both consistent and intermittent Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs) that have been triggered by the vehicle. The Freeze Frame Data helps the PQSS team track the vehicle's performance at the time the fault occurred, ensuring that quality issues are accurately identified and addressed. This data is instrumental in initiating recalls and offers valuable insights for quality forecasting, particularly for newer vehicle models. To access complete diagnostic information across multiple data types, including DTCs, FFD, and vehicle files, refer to the Service Connect Remote Vehicle Diagnostics API. To view vehicle usage patterns and customer behavior over time, please refer to the Driving Behavior Analytics API.

name: Finished Goods Shipment Confirmation
listdetail: This API transmits shipment confirmations from SAP to the Manufacturing Operations Management (MOM) system. It notifies that finished goods, having completed the manufacturing process, have been shipped and are en route to customers, retailers, or distribution centers. The confirmation is provided at the shipment level only and does not include item-level details or the contents of the shipment. The API allows Procurement and Inventory Management teams to track the movement of finished goods, monitor order fulfillment status, enhance visibility across the supply chain, and support accurate planning and inventory control. By ensuring timely and reliable shipment confirmation, it plays a key role in maintaining operational efficiency throughout the fulfillment process. The SAP Parts Master Reference API ensures all systems have consistent and up-to-date part definitions.

name: Enterprise Vehicle Profit Planning
platform: TBDP (IRM, PASA, C360, Q360, IRM-Pricing, etc.)
listdetail: This dataset contains CMBS/CMBK (Contribution Margin by Series and Katashiki) data for Enterprise Vehicle Profit analysis that can influence executives' daily and long-term decisions. CMBS/CMBK is an Excel application that combines information from pricing calculations and other sources to produce contribution margin reports by Series and Katashiki; it tracks contribution margins and installation rates down to option and specification levels. Based on these calculations, the company can measure its ability to cover variable costs with revenue. The Index of Profitability (IDX) was developed to mask data related to profits and trends so that Toyota Financial Services (TFS) could share this information with business partners without exposing sensitive information. This data is crucial for strategic volume decisions between sales, marketing, and production to evaluate the impact on profitability.

name: Engineering Change Instructions Tracking
listdetail: This API gives users access to the latest Engineering Change Instructions (ECIs) and associated part data, such as material specs, design details, drawings, and supplier information. By querying an ECI or Production Part Release (PPR) number, users can retrieve accurate, current details needed to track and manage engineering changes within the electronic Master Data Management (eMDM) system. Engineering changes can impact part quality, vehicle performance, and manufacturing efficiency. This API helps Toyota purchasing teams and suppliers reduce that risk by providing timely, reliable information. It also supports traceability through access to drawing records, minor code transitions, and historical registration data. To verify that a part is ready for use in vehicle builds, please refer to the Vehicle Parts Lifecycle Status API.

It enables updates to key profile fields and retrieves application-specific employee roles, detailing each role’s name, description, and corresponding IDs for effective role-based access control. By specifying cost center, plant, and date filters, users can retrieve real-time and historical data on time in/out punches, paid time off, and Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) counts. Designed for Group Leaders and management, the system provides easy access to key operational data, including exact entry and exit times via the Gate Check feature, helping with oversight, security, and leave management for efficient manufacturing operations.

name: Email Marketing Preferences
listdetail: This API manages email marketing preferences for Toyota and Lexus products and services in compliance with the Controlling the Assault of Non-Solicited Pornography And Marketing (CAN-SPAM) Act based on choices made by customers and prospective customers. This U.S. regulation sets the rules for sending commercial emails, grants recipients the right to opt out of future messages, and promotes responsible email marketing practices. Through this API, customer preferences such as opting in or out of marketing communications are captured and stored, enabling the customer marketing team to accurately distribute automated emails and promotions only to eligible consumers. It also ensures that customers who have unsubscribed are properly excluded from future email campaigns, helping maintain compliance and customer trust.

name: Electronic Control Unit Replacement Key Validation
listdetail: This API facilitates secure communication between Toyota systems during the reprogramming or replacement of a vehicle’s Electronic Control Unit (ECU). When a technician connects a Global Techstream (GTS) device to a vehicle, it sends safety key identifiers to Product Quality & Service Support (PQSS). PQSS then uses this API to request the corresponding Manual Allocation Code (MAC) key information from Toyota Motor Corporation (TMC). After TMC’s quality team authenticates the request, the necessary key data is returned, allowing authorization of a new or replacement ECU. This API ensures that the key exchange process is handled securely and efficiently, supporting accurate and authorized ECU updates. To access a list of ECU values for a specific VIN, including last acquisition mileage, date, ECU values, and network target address, consult the Service Connect Electronic Control Unit Values List API. For the outcome of monitored ECU values based on a VIN, view the Electronic Control Unit Monitoring Results API.

name: Electronic Control Unit Monitoring Results
listdetail: This API returns the outcome, or the result, of the monitored Electronic Control Unit (ECU) values based on the vehicle VIN. Improve vehicle service satisfaction by investigating or monitoring Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTC) without the vehicle being present. The Service Lane Portal (SLP) requests remote monitoring of sensors through Data Hub (DH) and returns VIN, ECU ID, ECU Name, and Monitoring Details. To view all DTCs not triggered by a maintenance event for a specific VIN in Data Hub (DH), refer to the Trouble Code Prioritization API. The Trouble Code Transmission for Maintenance Events API focuses on transmitting diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) that are triggered by specific maintenance events. For comprehensive remote vehicle diagnostics, including DTCs and Freeze Frame Data (FFD), refer to the Service Connect Remote Vehicle Diagnostics API. To access a list of ECU values for a specific VIN, including last acquisition mileage, date, ECU values, and network target address, consult the Service Connect Electronic Control Unit Values List API. To authorize the reprogramming or replacement of a vehicle's ECU, please refer to the Electronic Control Unit Replacement Key Validation API.

name: eBoM Reporting
listdetail: The Gold Standard Bill of Materials (BoM) Dashboard is comprised of reports that help in decision making through analysis of BoM structure and product (vehicle and non-vehicle) cost information. Reports are available on demand (on-line) and on a regular schedule. The on-online reports provide the DataMart refresh details and schedule report details - for the last run and for the next run. Also available are cumulative part usage and cost based on VIN and non-vehicle production data using the production date range supplied by the user and various reports summarizing differences between the eBoM system calculations and the General Ledger (GL) balances. The scheduled reports are used to compare two different costed BoM, schedule the HON report, report HON LE and MFG data to be used as input source to HON Hyperion Cube, schedule the standard BoM report for all vehicle and non-vehicle data, and schedule the uncosted BoM report for vehicle data.

The data provided through this API is primarily used to generate feedback and performance insights based on personal driving history, contributing to product quality enhancement and customer satisfaction initiatives. It functions independently from diagnostic fault-triggered services, offering ongoing or event-based behavioral data rather than responding to specific vehicle faults or maintenance events.

name: Demo Vehicle Indicator
listdetail: This API service is used by applications to convert the category of a vehicle in inventory to a Demo category (“L”). Demo vehicles are part of a dealer’s inventory, but they are labeled as Demo to allow the dealer to submit warranty claims for that VIN. For warranty eligibility, vehicles must be sold to a customer before they receive a Date of First Use, but Demo vehicles get a DOFU before they are sold. Dealers use Demo cars for test drives or special sales events, but ultimately sell them as new via the Retail Delivery Report (RDR) process just like any other new vehicle. As part of the Demo processing provided by this API, the odometer reading is provided by the dealer when the vehicle is converted to Demo.

name: Dealer Pricing
listdetail: Dealers can find the complete dealer pricing details for a vehicle with this API service. As part of the Vehicle Inquiry Service (VIS), Dealer Pricing Info can provide users with basic invoice information about the total price of a vehicle during wholesale from Toyota Motor North America (TMNA) a franchise dealer for the submitted VIN. The information returned includes the total invoice amount and a breakdown of items included in the invoice total such as the base model price and total cost of factory-installed (FIO) or post-processing options (PPO), dealer margins, freight and fuel charges, dealer advertising costs, and any discount information. The discount information includes a discount indicator to specify the type of discount and the discount amount applied to the vehicle price. For pricing information involving vehicle sales to private distributors Southeast Toyota Distributors LLC (SET) and Gulf Sales Toyota GST), please use the Distributor Pricing API. If you need pricing and details for vehicle accessories including availability and compatibility, please view the Dealer Accessory Pricing API.

name: Dealer Incentive Payment Inquiry
listdetail: This API provides dealers with real-time access to incentive payment details for completed programs. Through the Dealer Daily portal, dealers can input a vehicle series and retrieve authorized payments. Details include the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN), incentive category, program name, payment amount, method, and dates. Powered by Toyota’s Incentive Claims Administration Tool (iCAT), which processes incentive certificates and dealer challenge payments, this API supports payment verification, reconciliation, and reporting. It allows dealers to confirm received funds, helps accounting teams match payments with internal records, and enables OEM teams to track program performance and respond to inquiries efficiently. By integrating with internal systems, this API enhances transparency and streamlines financial operations related to dealer incentives.
